title: แตกต่างเหมือนกัน · Dtɛ̀ɛk-dtàang Mʉ̌an Gan (Different Too)
about: About choosing your own path while everyone judges it, and hoping to find someone who is 'different too'. Good timing: it uses today's question word + gɔ̂ɔ pattern twice, and doon, the casual passive.

lines.th: เลือกไปเพราะใจบอก
lines.en: I chose it because my heart told me to
lines.note: Subject dropped again (I chose). jai bɔ̀ɔk = 'the heart says', the Thai way of saying 'my gut told me'.

lines.r: lɛ́ɛo tammai mii krai dtɔ̀ɔ krai dtɔ̂ng kɔɔi dtàtsǐn
lines.th: แล้วทำไมมีใครต่อใครต้องคอยตัดสิน
lines.en: so why does everybody always have to judge
lines.note: krai dtɔ̀ɔ krai = everybody, all sorts of people. kɔɔi + verb = to keep doing it (kɔɔi also means 'to wait'). dtàtsǐn = to judge (you know dtàtsǐnjai = to decide).

lines.r: wâa taang nán man pìt, piang prɔ́ wâa man dtàang
lines.th: ว่าทางนั้นมันผิด เพียงเพราะว่ามันต่าง
lines.en: that the path is wrong, just because it's different
lines.note: man (it) is added before the adjective, very common in casual speech: man pìt, man dtàang. piang prɔ́ wâa = just because.

lines.r: dtɛ̀ɛ tam arai, sùttáai gɔ̂ɔ doon bòn
lines.th: แต่ทำอะไร สุดท้ายก็โดนบ่น
lines.en: but whatever I do, in the end I get nagged
lines.note: Today's pattern! tam arai … gɔ̂ɔ = whatever I do. doon = casual tùuk (passive for bad things): doon bòn (get nagged), doon dàa (get told off). sùttáai = in the end.

lines.r: dtɛ̀ɛ jà yùu tîi dtrong nǎi, gɔ̂ɔ mâi jəə gàp krai
lines.th: แต่จะอยู่ที่ตรงไหน ก็ไม่เจอกับใคร
lines.en: but wherever I am, I don't meet anyone
lines.note: Question word + gɔ̂ɔ again: dtrong nǎi … gɔ̂ɔ mâi … = wherever …, never …. dtrong nǎi is a casual 'where exactly'.

lines.th: มีใครสักคนไหม
lines.note: sàk + classifier = 'just one, at least one': krai sàk kon (someone, anyone), sàk wan (someday), sàk krûu (a moment).

lines.r: piang dtɔ̂nggaan kɛ̂ɛ krai sák kon jàp mʉʉ chán wái
lines.th: เพียงต้องการแค่ใครซักคนจับมือฉันไว้
lines.en: all I need is someone to hold my hand
lines.note: piang … kɛ̂ɛ = just, only (said twice for emphasis). ซัก (sák) is the casual spelling of สัก (sàk). verb + wái = to keep holding, keep in place.

words: เปลี่ยนแปลง
ไม่เคยหยุด
เพียงเพราะว่า
(casual) to get (something bad done to you)
notes: Two lines use today's question word + gɔ̂ɔ: 'tam arai … gɔ̂ɔ doon bòn' and 'yùu tîi dtrong nǎi gɔ̂ɔ mâi jəə gàp krai'. Listen for gɔ̂ɔ after a question word: it means 'whatever / wherever'.
doon is the everyday version of tùuk for bad things: doon bòn, doon dàa, doon mɛɛo gàt. You'll hear doon far more than tùuk in speech.
man (it) is used as an empty subject for situations and feelings: nai wan tîi man nʉ̀ai (on days when it's tiring), man dtàang (it's different).
Thai songs repeat half-lines ('kâo maa mâi kəəi yùt, kâo maa mâi kəəi yùt'). The repeats are a good place to sing along.
